entries.criterion: When I build a world, the build record shows that world's own bookkeeping laws in plain words, and they are right for that world: the AI that designs it uses what it knows (that buying means paying, that pencils have to be made).
grounded_in: Brian 2026-10-28: the AI that designs the world declares its laws (design part 1, approved "yes lets make it companhy plannign complaint")
demonstration: Open the World Builder.
Paste the pencil description and press Create simulation.
When the build finishes, open the build record and read the Laws list.
entries.expected: A short list of sentences in the pencil world's own words, such as "Pencils are made only by assembling them and used up only by a customer" and "A sale moves pencils to the buyer and cash to the seller", each naming things and moves that appear elsewhere on the page, and each one true of the world the description describes.
entries.failure_example: Broken: the Laws list is missing; a law names something the pencil world does not have (gold, a bank); a law is wrong for the world (cash may appear from any move, or a sale needs no payment); or the same laws appear word for word for a kitchen description. Working: every law names this world's goods, money and moves and says what the description implies.

representation.view: composite-linked-view: a laws table in the build record, each row opening the moves it names

entries.built_note: S1 (#280): the shared s3-pencil-4 run lists "Laws this world keeps" (scripts/world_builder_home.html:507); evidence/declared-laws/s3-pencil-4/TRACE_READ.md. Brian has not judged it.

entries.criterion: The engine itself keeps each world's declared laws: a move, or a knock-on effect it sets off, that breaks one is refused, and the page says which law it broke.
grounded_in: Brian 2026-10-28: the engine enforces declared laws generically and names the law it refuses on (design part 2)
demonstration: Open the World Builder's replay of the saved pencil13 world, re-built in S2 so that the world design AI wrote its laws (the S2 report gives the link and shows the laws came from the model reply, not a person).
Go to round 8 and find the shop's buy-boxed-pencils move; read what the page says about it.
Open the S2 report's second replay, a world whose move sets off a knock-on effect that breaks a law (for example a fall that would destroy cash), and read that round.
Share the pencil13 replay, open the shared link in a new window, and go back to round 8.
entries.expected: The purchase is marked refused (orange, with the word "refused") beside a law in plain words saying a purchase must move payment the other way; the shop's boxes and the factory's cash are unchanged that round. In the knock-on replay the move that set off the effect is refused the same way, the page names the knock-on effect that broke the law, and nothing from that moment is kept. The shared link shows the same refusal in the same round: the engine keeps it in the world's recorded history, with the moment that caused it.
entries.failure_example: Broken: the purchase shows as done, boxes move to the shop and no cash moves to the factory (what pencil13 does today); or it is refused with no law named; or the knock-on effect goes through and only the move is undone. Working: refused, law shown, nothing from the moment kept.

representation.view: composite-linked-view: the run's round list with the refusal row opening its law

entries.built_note: S2 (#284) engine refusal is built and tested (src/world_substrate/laws.py); the page view of a refusal naming its law has not been walked on a saved world, so this stays not built.

entries.criterion: An independent review points out where the rules do not match my description, in my description's words.
grounded_in: Brian 2026-10-28: an independent AI review of the rules replaces the heuristic checks (design part 3)
demonstration: Open the build record of the saved pencil13 world reviewed in S3 (link given in the S3 report).
Open the review panel: it shows what the reviewer was given (the description, the laws and the rules, nothing else) and which model reviewed, next to the model that wrote the rules.
Read the Review findings list.
entries.expected: The panel shows the reviewer got only the description, the laws and the rules, and a different model from the rules writer. Each finding names one rule and quotes the words of the description it was checked against; one finding says buy-boxed-pencils takes the boxes but pays the factory nothing.
entries.failure_example: Broken: the list is empty, says only "looks good", gives findings without quoting the description, or the panel shows the same model that wrote the rules, or the reviewer was given the rules writer's conversation. Working: a different model, the three inputs only, and buy-boxed-pencils named with the quoted description words.

representation.view: composite-linked-view: a findings table, each row opening its rule and the quoted words

entries.built_note: S3 (#291) review runs and its findings are saved in the share record (review_findings), but the page has no findings panel yet, so this stays not built.

entries.criterion: Moves are still written freely in each world's own terms; there is no fixed menu of move types.

entries.failure_example: Broken: every move is labelled with one of a few fixed kinds, or a move the description asks for (a cook tasting a sauce) cannot be written because no kind fits. Working: moves differ per world and the laws sit beside them.

entries.criterion: Descriptions the World Builder has never seen, of very different shapes and lengths, each build a world that keeps its own laws, with no code written for any of them.
grounded_in: Brian 2026-10-28: the root problems are in the substrate and the world generating and validating process, not one pencil world
Plan S5: four varied descriptions built live in parallel
demonstration: Open the World Builder and build each of four different descriptions in turn: the pencil supply chain, the airfield, a kitchen, and the long Waltzman scenario (people and organizations, not goods).
For each, open the build record's Laws and Review findings, then the run.
Open any refused step, and any sale or hand-over in the run.
entries.expected: Each of the four worlds has laws naming its own things and moves (the Waltzman world may declare few or none, and says so); every refused step names the law it broke, including knock-on effects; every hand-over that a law pairs moves both sides; the review's findings quote that description's own words; all four builds finish.
entries.failure_example: Broken: the laws are the pencil world's laws reworded, a step commits that breaks a listed law (goods appear with no listed move making them), or the build only works for pencils. Working: each description gets its own laws and the run keeps them.

representation.view: composite-linked-view: build record (laws, findings) linked to the run's round list

entries.criterion: Mistakes in a world's rules are fixed at the root, in the engine, the world design and the review that every world shares, not by patches for one world or by a growing list of hand-written checks, one per mistake.
grounded_in: Brian 2026-10-28: "you hjave been fixing symptoms not root problems"
demonstration: Open a finished build record on the World Builder and read the panel that says what checked the rules.
Open the S4 table on this plan's review page: each retired hand-written check, the incident it was added for, and what catches that incident now.

On this plan's review page, open each finished slice's row: it lists, in plain words, what changed and where (the engine's law check, the world design's laws, the review), and whether any change names one world.
entries.expected: The build record lists three kinds of checking only: the world's declared laws, the review's findings, and reports of what the test run saw. Each retired check in the S4 table points at a saved world where a law refusal or a review finding now catches its incident, and no new hand-written check was added for a new mistake. Every slice's changes sit in the parts all worlds share; none names pencils, the cafe or any other single world.
entries.failure_example: Broken: the build record still lists checks such as 'goods from nothing' or 'starved holders' guessing at meaning, or a new mistake found in S5 was fixed by adding another such check. Working: the new mistake is traced to a missing law or a review finding and fixed there. Also broken: a slice row lists a change that only applies to the pencil world.

representation.view: composite-linked-view: its table pane lists retired check, incident, saved world and what catches it now
